We ask how people delegate to a language model and whether industry returns track it. Anthropic Economic Index releases from {{< var design.release.r1 >}} to {{< var design.release.r6 >}}, conversations matched to O\*NET tasks, are aggregated to occupations, countries and {{< var design.n_industries >}} Fama–French industries under a pre-registered protocol ({{< var pap.tag >}}). H1, less delegation in high-education, high-wage occupations, is {{< var rq1.h1.decision_text >}}: its null is not rejected at {{< var rq1.holm.h1 >}}. H2, delegation rising within tasks, is {{< var rq1.h2.decision_text >}}: its rise is one step, at a change of classified-conversation base. H3, more checking where errors are costly, is {{< var rq1.h3.decision_text >}}: the null that γ is zero is not rejected. H4, country differences beyond task mix, is {{< var rq1.h4.decision_text >}}. Industry delegation and human-rated theoretical exposure have Spearman ρ = {{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.rho >}} [{{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.ci.lo >}}, {{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.ci.hi >}}], partly through shared weights and zero-assigned unpublished occupations. The market test's minimum detectable effect exceeds D11's plausibility threshold, {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp, so market evidence is reported as what it can and cannot yet say: H5 is {{< var rq3.h5.decision_text >}} and H5b is {{< var rq3.h5b.decision_text >}} (H0: b = b̄; intervals [{{< var rq3.h5.ci_005.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5.ci_005.hi_pp2 >}}] and [{{< var rq3.h5b.ci_005.lo_pp2 >}}, {{< var rq3.h5b.ci_005.hi_pp2 >}}]; {{< var power.power_pct >}}% power only against a departure of at least {{< var rq3.h5.mde >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde >}} pp of annualised alpha per SD; verbatim in @sec-markets). Employment weights postdate formation: RQ2, H5 and H5b are out of sample in AEI data only, not strictly real-time (R32 real-time; R1 look-ahead). No robustness row changes a decision (@sec-robustness).
